> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Approving at 867b5fc6.

I reproduced the bug on main with a built CLI: `recall maintenance --prune --threshold abc` exits 0, reports the knowledge base as healthy and keeps the learning. At this head it exits 1 with `✖ --threshold must be a finite number`, and the learning stays. The default 0.15 and decimal values behave the same on both builds.

Hidden scope: none. The refusal is the fix itself. No default, flag or other output changes.

[P2 non-blocking] `Number()` accepts notations that `parseFloat` did not. `--threshold 0x10` used to read as 0 and prune nothing. Now it reads as 16, which prunes every learning:

```
Number('0x10') === 16    parseFloat('0x10') === 0
Number('0b1')  === 1     parseFloat('0b1')  === 0
```

Nobody is likely to type that, but it can delete files. A decimal-only test, as `parseIntOption` in `src/cli-int.ts` does for integers, would close it. So would refusing values outside 0..1, since a confidence above 1 prunes everything anyway.

[P3 nit] The parser could sit beside `parseIntOption` in `src/cli-int.ts` instead of inline in `index.ts`.

The CI review found nothing. I agree, apart from the notation point above.
